note: The team's own records of the members of Petto before the bot counted its members (2026, from the owner's spreadsheet). `baseline` are the members that stayed: dated anchors, a straight line for each day between two anchors (a jump is two anchors on consecutive days), and from the last anchor a straight line to today's live total; it has no noise added. `spikes` are the largest totals of single events: big communities that added the bot and removed it again (one of 246,000 members removed it the same day after a raid). A spike holds its total on the recorded day and the following days up to `spikeDays` (the bot was down, so they were not counted day by day), and then the baseline resumes. Assumed, because the owner gave no exact date or length: the date of the bottom of the baseline (2026-09-15, `assumed`) and the length of every spike (3 days, `spikeDays`, the owner said 3 days at most). Nothing is shown before the first anchor. Every day built from these records is marked `estimated` and they are only used for the days before the first snapshot the bot stored itself. `recorded` are exact counts the owner kept for the last days (55,700 on 2026-11-01 and 56,430 after it; the date 2026-11-03 for the second is assumed): from the first of them to today the days are drawn as real, not estimated.

activityBaseline.note: The messages, reactions and voice time the bot counted before the outage of Discord are in `globalStatsBaseline` (config.js) as one total. For the daily history they are spread as a flat average over these days (from the first day of the records to the day before the outage), on top of what activity_stats really counted on each of them. It is approximate: the real day by day numbers were lost. The days of the outage week and every later day are shown exactly as counted.
